summary: The pure aggregator aggregateDesignerTimesheetCosts() is well-tested and mostly correct, but the wiring in designerTimesheetReport() has a real data-completeness bug in a financial Budget-vs-Actual feature: byDesignerStatus silently drops the budget amount for any designer who has a pms_budget_line_items row but zero time entries anywhere in the org (e.g. a newly budgeted designer who hasn't logged hours yet, or one who left before logging any), because designerStatusByUser is built only from entries, not from the full user roster already fetched as allUsers -- so sum(byDesignerStatus.budget) silently diverges from overallBudget in a plausible, non-rare real-world state, with no error surfaced. Separately, designerTimesheetReport() now calls resolveBillableRate() (a DB round-trip that itself re-fetches and filters the org's full pmsBillableRates table) once per time entry inside a sequential for-loop over every time entry in the entire org (not just this project), even though this exact file's own pms-time-service.ts already exposes a pure, pre-fetch-once variant (resolvePmsBillableRatePure) for this precise reason -- a real, avoidable N+1 that could make this report slow to the point of timing out for orgs with meaningful time-entry volume. The response also silently mixes project-scoped fields (byCategory, byDesignerStatus) with org-wide fields (byDesigner, byProject) under a single designerTimesheetReport(projectId) contract with no field-level indication of scope, which is likely to mislead a per-project report UI. None of this is a security or tenant-isolation issue (org scoping via ctx.orgId/withTenantContext is intact throughout, requireConstructionEnabled still gates access), but the budget-undercount bug is a real correctness defect in a report whose entire purpose is accurate budget-vs-actual totals, so this should go back for a fix rather than merge as-is.
issues: byDesignerStatus in aggregateDesignerTimesheetCosts (construction-reports-service.ts) computes designerStatusByUser only from the `entries` array; a pms_budget_line_items row for a userId with zero time entries anywhere in the org is excluded from both the active and inactive buckets, so sum(byDesignerStatus.budget) can be less than overallBudget with no indication anything was dropped. designerTimesheetReport() already fetches allUsers (with isActive) and could pass that roster in to fix this.

designerTimesheetReport() calls the DB-querying resolveBillableRate() once per time entry inside a sequential for-loop over ALL of the org's pms_time_entries (not just this project's), each call independently re-fetching and filtering the full pmsBillableRates table -- a real N+1 that this same file's pms-time-service.ts already solves via the pure resolvePmsBillableRatePure(rates, userId, asOf), which should be used with a single upfront rates fetch instead.

byDesigner and byProject are computed org-wide while byCategory and byDesignerStatus are scoped to the requested projectId, all returned under the same designerTimesheetReport(ctx, projectId) call with no field-level indication of which breakdowns are project-scoped vs org-wide -- likely to mislead a per-project report UI into showing a designer's or another project's org-wide totals as if they belonged to the requested project.
